title: Why Study Earth From Space?

cues.text: Have you ever wondered how we can tell whether a forest is shrinking, a town is growing, or a lake is changing over time?
One way is to look at Earth from space.
Satellites travel around our planet and collect information about its surface and atmosphere.
They help us observe large areas that would be difficult to study from the ground alone.
This is useful here in Ghana.
Satellite images can help researchers monitor vegetation, study flooding, observe changes in settlements, and investigate patterns in water and land use.
An important advantage is that satellites can observe the same places repeatedly.
By comparing images from different dates, we can identify changes that might otherwise go unnoticed.
However, an image does not always tell us why something changed.
Clouds, seasons, shadows, and differences in image processing can affect what we see.
Sometimes, researchers need measurements from the ground to understand the full story.
In this course, you will learn how satellites observe Earth and how to begin exploring real satellite imagery.
